title: Slimline Air-Gap & Network Contract for Private VPC Deploys
creator: Aisha Malhotra
summary: Define a minimal, reviewable contract for network, upgrade, and air-gap constraints that allows customers to run Redwood Private in highly restricted VPCs with an approval-grade acceptance criteria set. This ticket balances operator surface area and strict offline constraints while enabling a repeatable upgrade path for customers with limited egress.
background: Multiple enterprise customers have requested a formally scoped network/upgrade contract that (1) documents exactly what outbound connectivity is required during bootstrap and upgrades, (2) defines a slim offline artifact distribution option for fully air-gapped sites, and (3) specifies acceptance criteria operators and SREs can use to verify a safe upgrade. Existing PRDs are broad and overlap; this ticket consolidates a compact, auditable contract to unblock legal/security reviews and sales engineering commitments.
goals: 1) Produce a one-page network contract that teams can sign off on. 2) Define upgrade acceptance criteria (canary/pass/fallback) for sealed VPCs. 3) Specify an air-gap artifact distribution mode with deterministic checksum verification. 4) Produce operator runbook snippets for emergency rollback and monitoring thresholds.
non_goals: 1) Implementation work for a new operator CLI. 2) Designing alternative transport protocols (e.g., custom P2P). 3) Replacing the full private deploy architecture — this is contract + acceptance criteria only.
constraints:
- Must fit within current operator and image signing tooling.
- No permanent open inbound ports.
- Minimize prerequisite services (ideally allow one-time egress during bootstrap or rely on customer-hosted mirror).
- Changes must be compatible with existing Dedicated and Hosted compatibility profiles for simple customer migrations.
requirements:
1) Network: Define exact IP ranges, FQDNs, and ports that may be opened temporarily during bootstrap and upgrades and enumerate an explicit minimal allowlist.
2) Upgrade: Specify staged upgrade flow (canary node, operator / staged mirror, automatic rollback predicates).
3) Air-gap artifact distribution: Provide manifest format, signing verification steps, and operator checksums.
4) Observability: Minimum telemetry/health signals we require during and after upgrade (agent heartbeat, version stamp, artifact provenance).
5) Security: KMS interaction requirements (when KMS rotation occurs) and guidance for handling KMS/HSM in offline mode.
6) Acceptance artifacts: Example test plan scripts and datasets to validate model-serving correctness and KV cache integrity after upgrade.
acceptance_criteria:
1) Network contract doc signed by Security and Solutions Engineering: states exact egress FQDNs and ports and under what windows (one-time bootstrap vs upgrade window).
2) Upgrade test: Execute a staged upgrade in a sealed VPC lab that follows the contract; canary instance must serve traffic and pass smoke tests for 6 hours; rollback must complete and restore prior version within SLA (30 minutes).
3) Air-gap verification: Customer-provided mirror can be used to perform a full install and upgrade without any outbound connectivity; all images and manifests validate with image-signing checksums.
4) Operator runbook: Playbook for rollback, forensic logs extraction, and post-mortem template exists and is linked.
5) Minimal metrics: Console dashboard shows per-node version, artifact provenance, and upgrade progress; alerting thresholds for tokenization/latency regressions are present.
6) Security review complete and documented in ticket comments and Confluence.
rollout_strategy:
- Phase 0: Validate contract with internal sealed-vpc lab (greenfield).
- Phase 1: Run contract against two pilot customers in non-critical namespaces.
- Phase 2: Expand to broader customer set after pilot sign-off.
- For each phase: require signed acceptance from customer SRE and Redwood solutions engineer before scheduling upgrades.
upgrade_compatibility:
- Support upgrades where images can be staged into a customer mirror ahead of time.
- Backward-compatible control-plane interactions: when full control-plane access is not available, operator must rely on manifest-based verification only.
- Fallback: if canary fails health checks, automatic rollback within 30 minutes is mandatory.
- In cases where auto-rollback fails, we must provide a documented manual recovery path and post-mortem steps.
network_topology_requirements:
- Recommended topology: private subnet with NAT gateway for one-time egress or a customer mirror inside same VPC/subnet.
- Allowlist (minimal): outbound HTTPS to artifacts.redwood-inference.com (443), control-plane ephemeral mirror endpoints (list will be published), and customer KMS endpoints.
- No inbound external ports allowed; operator-to-node connections must be initiated from inside the VPC.
- If customer uses HTTP proxies, document CONNECT/TLS pass-through list and certificate pinning guidance.
airgap_artifact_distributor:
- Manifest format: JSON list of image digests, tarballs, and signed release notes.
- Signing: All artifacts must be signed using Redwood image-signing key; operator must verify signatures and SHA256 checksums.
- Distribution modes: (A) USB / physical media fallback (operator-assisted import script), (B) Customer-hosted mirror, (C) staged mirror via a pre-approved temporary NAT window.
- Verification: operator-run 'airgap-verify' script which returns pass/fail and writes notarization record to local audit log.
observability_and_operational_playbook:
- Dashboards: upgrade-progress, per-node version, artifact provenance, and latency/error regressions.
- Alerts: failure-to-start, checksum-mismatch, heartbeat-loss >5m, canary-traffic-error-rate >0.5% sustained 10m.
- Playbook sections: pre-upgrade checklist, canary verification steps, rollback steps, post-upgrade validation, customer-acceptance sign-off template.
security_and_kms:
- KMS integration modes: online (Redwood KMS endpoint), proxy-to-customer-KMS, or offline KMS token import.
- For air-gapped sites using offline KMS token import, document TTLs and rotation guidance; rotate KMS tokens during scheduled maintenance windows only.
- Image provenance: all images must include signed SBOM and attestations prior to acceptance.
- Audit log retention and export: provide guidance for customers to export operator logs in a tamper-evident format.
migration_and_testing_plan:
- Create a sealed-vpc lab that mirrors customer constraints.
- Test cases: fresh-install, staged-upgrade (minor), staged-upgrade (major), rollback-on-failure, mirror-sync failure handling.
- Test data sets: small prompt set to validate generation quality and a KV cache exercise suite to validate state migration.
- Define success criteria: deterministic start/stop, checksum match of artifacts, and smoke API test pass rate >99% over 6 hours.
risks_and_mitigations:
- Risk: Customer mirror lag causes partial upgrades. Mitigation: pre-stage images and require mirror sync verification before upgrade window.
- Risk: Manual media transfer induces human error. Mitigation: provide deterministic import script and checksum verification with signed manifests.
- Risk: KMS rotation during upgrade window. Mitigation: require rotation freeze during upgrade windows or pre-authorized rotation tokens.
decisions:
- Chosen a slim, auditable contract limited to required egress endpoints rather than an open-ended policy.
- Require signed manifests for air-gap installs; physical media allowed but must go through the importer script for checksum verification.
- Canary window set to 6 hours for pilot phase; may be tuned after pilot feedback.
outstanding_questions:
1) Should we allow customers to specify custom image-signing keys instead of Redwood signing? (security trade-off).
2) Is 30-minute rollback SLA acceptable for all enterprise customers?
3) Do we require mandatory SBOM publication for every release in the staged mirror path?
4) Edge-case: partial mirror sync during multi-cluster upgrades — should operator enforce global pause?
